classification.difficultyReason: Count the shared and external fencing, express the pen length in terms of its width, and substitute into the total area.

content.prompt:
A farmer uses 200 m of fencing to create four adjacent rectangular pens of equal size. Each pen has width $x$ metres (perpendicular to the shared sides).

Show that the total enclosed area is $A=160x-\dfrac{32x^2}{5}$.

spec.description: An upright rectangle divided into four equal adjacent pens by three full-height vertical lines. No dimension labels or shading.
spec.mathematics: Four equal widths perpendicular to five parallel fence segments; the external top and bottom each span four pen widths. Drawing coordinates express topology and illustrative proportions only.
spec.answerVisibility: All outlines are permanent student-visible givens; no solution annotations.

answer.worked:
Let the length of each pen be $\ell$ metres. The fencing consists of two lengths of $4x$ and five lengths of $\ell$.

$$\begin{align*}2(4x)+5\ell&=200\\\ell&=\frac{200-8x}{5}\\\ell&=40-\frac{8x}{5}\end{align*}$$

The total area of the four pens is

$$\begin{align*}A&=4x\ell\\A&=4x\left(40-\frac{8x}{5}\right)\\A&=160x-\frac{32x^2}{5}\text{ m}^2.\end{align*}$$
